messages:
maria-cs: hi folks — customer (ACME) reported a user got deprovisioned unexpectedly after a bulk group rename from Okta. They say the user was still in another group that should map to the same role, but in our UI the account shows as removed. can we triage? :eyes:

dan-eng: thanks, digging in. do we have the SCIM logs/IDs from ACME? ask them to send the Okta provisioning logs if possible. sounds like a group->role mapping flip.

maria-cs: pasted the Okta webhook sequence they provided. timestamps are approximate. they said this started around 2025-08-21 17:22:10 UTC.

maria-cs (paste):
```
2025-08-21T17:22:10Z PUT /scim/v2/Groups/00a1...   200 OK  req_id=rid-abc123
2025-08-21T17:22:11Z PATCH /scim/v2/Users/281b...  200 OK  req_id=rid-abc124  // membership add: groupA -> user
2025-08-21T17:22:11Z DELETE /scim/v2/Groups/00a1... 204 No Content req_id=rid-abc125 // group rename/delete race
2025-08-21T17:22:12Z PATCH /scim/v2/Users/281b...  200 OK  req_id=rid-abc126  // later membership patch showing empty members
2025-08-21T17:22:13Z POST /internal/prov/eval  500 err=role-resolve-failed req_id=rid-abc127
```

dan-eng: hmm that sequence looks like we processed the group delete before the user membership add finished. our role resolution code currently treats 'group not found' as a removal candidate and may schedule deprovision if no other role found.

priya-sre: logs from our side for the user 281b... (sanitized):
```
[2025-08-21T17:22:11.102Z] prov.eval request rid-abc124 payload: { "id": "281b...", "memberships": ["groupA"] }
[2025-08-21T17:22:11.305Z] groups.delete handler rid-abc125 groupId=00a1... displayName="Engineering - EU" -> deleted
[2025-08-21T17:22:12.010Z] prov.eval request rid-abc126 payload: { "id": "281b...", "memberships": [] }
[2025-08-21T17:22:13.001Z] role.assign evaluated -> no role -> schedule deprovision job job=del-791
[2025-08-21T17:22:13.045Z] job.del-791 executed -> user set active=false
```

priya-sre: root cause appears to be a race in event ordering: Okta sent a PATCH to add membership and almost concurrently deleted the group object (Okta sometimes does delete + recreate on renames). our ingestion pipeline applies events as they arrive and the delete arrived before the later membership patch that ended up clearing the membership list. between those two points our role resolver saw an empty set and deprovisioned.

maria-cs: customer insists they didn't intend the user to be removed — the user should have remained via another group mapping. They also mentioned both groups shared the same displayName across two Okta apps, so Okta did a cross-app merge and sent ambiguous IDs.

dan-eng: two angles: 1) mapping by group id instead of displayName gives robustness — we already map by externalId when present, but if externalId collides or Okta reuses ids across apps we can be inconsistent. 2) defensive deprovision: don't immediately deprovision on transient empty membership; debounce for N seconds and reconcile with the authoritative SCIM list for the user.

priya-sre: agree. quick mitigation we can suggest to the customer: temporarily disable the group-to-role mapping for the affected role so we don't auto-deprovision while they fix Okta side, or enable a safety flag in our console: "require confirmation for deprovision" (we can toggle per-tenant).

maria-cs: customer asked for a timeline and a clear repro so they can change the Okta flow. can you add repro steps we can send them? they want to test in a sandbox before touching prod.

dan-eng: repro steps (draft):
1) Create two Okta apps A and B in the same tenant.
2) Create Group X in app A (externalId GXA), Group Y in app B (externalId GYB) but set both displayName="Engineering - EU".
3) Add user U to Group X. confirm our SCIM user shows membership [GXA] -> role resolves to "engineer".
4) Trigger an Okta admin action that renames Group X by deleting and recreating it in app A (Okta often does delete+create on rename). Okta may emit DELETE for GXA and then CREATE for new group GXA2.
5) In a narrow timing window, issue a PATCH membership update from app B that adds user U to Group Y, but make the DELETE race with the membership PATCH so our ingestion sees: PUT group delete -> user membership empty -> later membership patch clears members.
6) Observe: if delete arrives before the final membership snapshot, our pipeline will temporarily see no matching groups and schedule deprovision.

dan-eng: to capture the race locally use a proxy (ngrok) to delay one of the Okta requests by 200-500ms. also capture req_ids and timestamps. attach the SCIM payloads. example membership PATCH payload:
```
PATCH /scim/v2/Users/281b...
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [
    {"op": "replace", "path": "memberships", "value": [] }
  ]
}
```

priya-sre: proposed code changes:
- change role-resolver to consult a short-lived write-ahead state for recent events per user and delay deprovision decisions for 30s unless explicit delete intent present.
- when a group delete is processed, mark group as "deleted:pending" for 10s and delay any role impact until downstream membership snapshots are processed.
- add telemetry counters for 'provisioning_racy_deprovision' for detection.

dan-eng: I'll open a PR with the debounce + pending-delete behaviour and tests simulating interleaved events. will include a migration to add telemetry and a console toggle behind a feature flag. estimate: 3 days dev + 1 day QA.

maria-cs: perfect. i'll send the repro steps and recommended temporary mitigation to ACME, include the ticket link and ask them to run the sandbox repro and share logs.

deploy-bot: build triggered: prov-debounce-feature branch -> CI started (check: unit + integration)

priya-sre: follow-up: we should also recommend customer to ensure Okta sends membership snapshots after a rename instead of delete+create where possible, and prefer stable externalIds. i'll add a short note to the KB article about "SCIM rename patterns and race conditions".

maria-cs: thanks everyone, i'll update the ticket once ACME confirms sandbox repro. :thumbsup:
